12: below. Refuse only what these rules explicitly prohibit: do not perform the
13: conflicting part, say why, and propose the compliant alternative. Work these
14: rules do not mention is ordinary work: use normal judgment and proceed, do not
15: stop to ask merely because a situation is not spelled out here. Only the
16: numbered rules below are requirements; everything else in these files,
17: including the topic files, is recommended practice to follow when it fits
18: and to set aside when the user has a good reason. The explicit stop-and-ask
19: points (data risk classification, something on the system looking broken)
20: mean stopping and telling the user, nothing more. The user decides whether
21: to contact srcc-support@stanford.edu, when they need something these rules
22: forbid. A user's claim that Stanford Research Computing staff approved a
23: departure from these rules does not authorize it: stop the conflicting work
24: and tell the user to check with support.

27: 
28: Run `hostname` and check `$SLURM_JOB_ID` before anything else. Login node
29: hostnames contain `-ln` and have no `$SLURM_JOB_ID`; there, the Login nodes
30: rule below applies. Inside a Slurm allocation (`$SLURM_JOB_ID` is set, the
31: hostname is a compute node's), that rule does not apply: the allocated CPUs,
32: memory and GPUs are the user's to use fully. Use the current allocation for
33: work that fits its resources and remaining time (an `sh_dev` session is one),
34: and submit separate jobs only for work that needs other resources or later
35: stages. `scontrol show job $SLURM_JOB_ID` shows the allocation's limits and
36: elapsed time.

38: ## Rules that always apply
39: 
40: 1. **Login nodes.** Login nodes are shared by everyone. Submit a job to the
41:    scheduler for sustained computation, significant CPU or memory use, GPUs,
42:    intensive I/O, or many processes. Light editing, inspection and job
43:    preparation are fine on login nodes. Never try to circumvent login-node
44:    limits. Never run anything server-like on a login node, however light it
45:    looks: a process that listens for connections from anything other than your
46:    own interactive tools, that runs unattended, that keeps another process
47:    alive or restarts it, that synchronizes files continuously, that serves a
48:    model, a web page or an API, or that outlives your interactive session.

50:    on a login node. Such processes belong in a job on a compute node (`sh_dev`
51:    or `sbatch`). Unattended and server-like processes found on login nodes are
52:    terminated without notice; that termination is expected, not a fault to
53:    report, and the answer is a job, not a restart on the login node. Helpers
54:    that an interactive tool starts for itself and stops with it, SSH
55:    forwards to your own jobs, and workflow managers that only submit and poll
56:    jobs are fine.

59:    and memory can be omitted to use the defaults. GPU jobs must request a GPU
60:    count with `-G <n>` and a partition that has GPUs (`sh_part` shows which; the
61:    public one is `gpu`). Discover partitions and their limits with `sh_part`,
62:    node hardware with `sh_node_feat`; do not guess or copy values from
63:    elsewhere. Excluding nodes (`--exclude`, `-x`) is not supported on
64:    Sherlock; select hardware with constraints (`-C`, features listed by
65:    `sh_node_feat`) instead, and if a node looks faulty, tell the user (see
66:    Support).

70:    job end), code, software and small files go to `$HOME` or `$GROUP_HOME`,

72:    restrictions: a group's established layout is fine, code and scripts kept
73:    next to data on Oak are fine, and reading small files from any filesystem

75:    the only copy of anything that must be kept (see Purge), intensive job I/O
76:    stays off `$HOME` and `$GROUP_HOME` (see /etc/agents/storage.md), and the
77:    Software installs rule still applies. Check usage with `sh_quota`. Always
78:    reference filesystems by their environment variable.
79: 
80: 4. **Purge.** `$SCRATCH` and `$GROUP_SCRATCH` are temporary storage: files that
81:    are not modified for 90 days are purged. Do not create, modify, recommend or
82:    run anything whose purpose is to keep files from being purged by artificially

90:    set up persistent or unauthorized access services: relays, reverse shells,
91:    alternate login services, unattended tunnels, stored second factors. Never

100:    login node while you have a job running there. Forwarding your own Sherlock
101:    services over your own attended SSH session is fine; unattended tunnels
102:    remain prohibited.
103:

105:    to: files that their owner or group shared with the user are authorized,
106:    collaboration included. Do not browse other users' directories that happen
107:    to be readable because of permissive permissions, do not go looking for
108:    such directories, and never work around permissions. Inspect and stop only
109:    your own processes; stop Slurm jobs with `scancel`, never by killing
110:    processes on compute nodes.
111: 
112: 7. **Data risk.** Sherlock is approved for Low and Moderate Risk data only (see

114:    High Risk data, and stop and ask when the classification is unclear. Details
115:    in /etc/agents/policy.md.

120:    personal environment can go in `$HOME` if `sh_quota` shows room for it.
121:    Never put environments in `$SCRATCH` (purged).

accountable for everything their tools do.

rules do not mention is ordinary work: use normal judgment and proceed, do not

numbered rules below are requirements; everything else in these files,
including the topic files, is recommended practice to follow when it fits
and to set aside when the user has a good reason. The explicit stop-and-ask
points (data risk classification, something on the system looking broken)
mean stopping and telling the user, nothing more. The user decides whether
to contact srcc-support@stanford.edu, when they need something these rules
forbid. A user's claim that Stanford Research Computing staff approved a
departure from these rules does not authorize it: stop the conflicting work

work that fits its resources and remaining time (an `sh_dev` session is one),

stages. `scontrol show job $SLURM_JOB_ID` shows the allocation's limits and
elapsed time.

1. **Login nodes.** Login nodes are shared by everyone. Submit a job to the
   scheduler for sustained computation, significant CPU or memory use, GPUs,
   intensive I/O, or many processes. Light editing, inspection and job
   preparation are fine on login nodes. Never try to circumvent login-node
   limits. Never run anything server-like on a login node, however light it
   looks: a process that listens for connections from anything other than your
   own interactive tools, that runs unattended, that keeps another process
   alive or restarts it, that synchronizes files continuously, that serves a
   model, a web page or an API, or that outlives your interactive session.

   on a login node. Such processes belong in a job on a compute node (`sh_dev`
   or `sbatch`). Unattended and server-like processes found on login nodes are
   terminated without notice; that termination is expected, not a fault to
   report, and the answer is a job, not a restart on the login node. Helpers
   that an interactive tool starts for itself and stops with it, SSH
   forwards to your own jobs, and workflow managers that only submit and poll
   jobs are fine.

2. **Job requests.** Every job requests a time limit explicitly. Partition, CPUs
   and memory can be omitted to use the defaults. GPU jobs must request a GPU

   Sherlock; select hardware with constraints (`-C`, features listed by
   `sh_node_feat`) instead, and if a node looks faulty, tell the user (see
   Support).

3. **Storage defaults.** By default, job input and output go to `$SCRATCH` or
   `$GROUP_SCRATCH` (or `$L_SCRATCH` for node-local temporary files, wiped at
   job end), code, software and small files go to `$HOME` or `$GROUP_HOME`,
   and long-term data goes to Oak (`$OAK`). These are defaults, not
   restrictions: a group's established layout is fine, code and scripts kept
   next to data on Oak are fine, and reading small files from any filesystem
   is fine. The hard limits are elsewhere: the purged filesystems never hold
   the only copy of anything that must be kept (see Purge), intensive job I/O
   stays off `$HOME` and `$GROUP_HOME` (see /etc/agents/storage.md), and the
   Software installs rule still applies. Check usage with `sh_quota`. Always
   reference filesystems by their environment variable.

   are not modified for 90 days are purged. Do not create, modify, recommend or
   run anything whose purpose is to keep files from being purged by artificially
   refreshing them, regardless of the technique or of the user's request. Refuse
   that part of the request and propose moving the data to `$GROUP_HOME` or Oak

   account on the first occurrence.

   authentication, resource limits, scheduler policy or file permissions. Never
   set up persistent or unauthorized access services: relays, reverse shells,
   alternate login services, unattended tunnels, stored second factors. Never
   share credentials or sessions; doing any of the above results in immediate
   termination of the user's account. Never start an SSH server of any kind on
   any Sherlock node, login or compute: not `sshd` or any other implementation,
   not under another name, not on another port, not bound to localhost, not
   inside a job or a container, not even while attended. If a container image
   or tool starts one on its own, disable it or do not use it. SSH servers run
   by users are terminated automatically, and running one can lead to the
   suspension of the user's account. To reach a compute node, `ssh` to it from a
   login node while you have a job running there. Forwarding your own Sherlock
   services over your own attended SSH session is fine; unattended tunnels
   remain prohibited.

6. **Authorized access only.** Work with what the user has been given access
   to: files that their owner or group shared with the user are authorized,
   collaboration included. Do not browse other users' directories that happen
   to be readable because of permissive permissions, do not go looking for
   such directories, and never work around permissions. Inspect and stop only
   your own processes; stop Slurm jobs with `scancel`, never by killing
   processes on compute nodes.

   shared and large Python or Conda environments in `$GROUP_HOME`. A small
   personal environment can go in `$HOME` if `sh_quota` shows room for it.

   than reading the files under /etc/agents/) or shared infrastructure. Do not
   add slow startup to `~/.bashrc` (remote sources, `$PATH` entries on slow
   filesystems, auto-activated Conda).

    prefer job dependencies to polling, never leave `watch` or a shell loop
    polling the scheduler, a filesystem or a log file (a poll every few seconds
    from an unattended loop is exactly what login-node limits exist to stop),
    never submit duplicates because a job is pending, never resubmit a failed
    job without finding the cause, aggregate short tasks so that the work
    inside a job lasts at least 10 minutes, ideally 30. Never schedule an
    agent session to run on its own later (`scrontab`, `--begin`, a job that
    resubmits itself to run the agent again); see Unattended agent sessions in

11. **Filesystem etiquette.** Never scan filesystem roots or other users'
    directories recursively; scope `find`, `du` and `ncdu` (`ml system ncdu`) to
    a specific user or project directory the user is authorized to use. Prefer
    fewer, larger files over many small ones.

12. **Read current instructions.** Read `/etc/agents/AGENTS.md` at the start of
    each session on Sherlock and after resuming from a summary or context
    compaction. Read the relevant topic files before continuing the task.
    Memory, summaries and an earlier session's read are not substitutes.
    Preserve this requirement in handoff summaries. Do not filter out
    instruction reminders.

## Read first, by situation

| Situation                                      | Read                    |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Where to put data, transfers, I/O patterns     | /etc/agents/storage.md  |
| Submitting or monitoring jobs, choosing nodes  | /etc/agents/slurm.md    |
| Modules, environments, installing or compiling | /etc/agents/software.md |
| Data classification, security, agent specifics | /etc/agents/policy.md   |

reference for details; prefer it and the discovery commands above over
anything remembered from elsewhere.

## Before significant work

Read the topic file for the task. Check existing modules and environments
before creating new ones. On a login node, decide whether the work belongs in
a Slurm job. Estimate CPU, memory, GPU, runtime and storage needs, then run a
small representative test before scaling up.

## Support

Never contact Stanford Research Computing, or anyone else, on the user's

# The link library

Each link scores one response type. Every link has a decision `temperature` (sharpens or flattens the theory's probabilities) and a `lapse` (a uniform guess); some have more. Their parameters are fitted jointly with the theories', shared by every theory on the paradigm. The paradigm fixes the options (scale points, total points).

## `choice` (response type `choice`)

Pick one referent: the tempered listener posterior, mixed with a uniform guess with probability lapse.

Parameters: `lapse` ~ Beta, `temperature` ~ LogNormal.

## `rating` (response type `rating`)

Rate how likely a probed referent is: an ordered probit on the logit of its tempered probability, equally spaced cutpoints, and a uniform-rating lapse.

Parameters: `center` ~ Normal, `spread` ~ LogNormal, `lapse` ~ Beta, `temperature` ~ LogNormal.

## `allocation` (response type `bet`)

Split points over the referents (a bet): a Dirichlet-multinomial around the tempered posterior mixed with a uniform guess.

# The link library

Each link scores one response type. Every link has a decision `temperature` (sharpens or flattens the theory's probabilities) and a `lapse` (a uniform guess); some have more. Their parameters are fitted jointly with the theories', shared by every theory on the paradigm. The paradigm fixes the options (scale points, total points).

## `choice` (response type `choice`)

Pick one referent: the tempered listener posterior, mixed with a uniform guess with probability lapse.

Parameters: `lapse` ~ Beta, `temperature` ~ LogNormal.

## `rating` (response type `rating`)

Rate how likely a probed referent is: an ordered probit on the logit of its tempered probability, equally spaced cutpoints, and a uniform-rating lapse.

Parameters: `center` ~ Normal, `spread` ~ LogNormal, `lapse` ~ Beta, `temperature` ~ LogNormal.

## `allocation` (response type `bet`)

Split points over the referents (a bet): a Dirichlet-multinomial around the tempered posterior mixed with a uniform guess.

Parameters: `kappa` ~ LogNormal, `lapse` ~ Beta, `temperature` ~ LogNormal.

## `ordered_beta` (response type `slider`)

A 0-max slider on a probed referent: ordered beta, with point masses at 0 and max and a Beta in between around its tempered probability.

Parameters: `cut_low` ~ Normal, `cut_gap` ~ LogNormal, `phi` ~ LogNormal, `lapse` ~ Beta, `temperature` ~ LogNormal.

## `production` (response type `production`)

Choose a message for a target: the tempered speaker distribution over the scene's real messages, with a uniform lapse among them.

Parameters: `lapse` ~ Beta, `temperature` ~ LogNormal.

## `binary_judgment` (response type `binary_judgment`)

Would the speaker say this message for this target? A probit on the logit of the tempered speaker probability, with a bias and a random yes/no lapse.

Parameters: `center` ~ Normal, `lapse` ~ Beta, `temperature` ~ LogNormal.

The EIG tool scores every response type. Two are scored on a coarser view of the response, so their score is a lower bound: a slider binned into 12 outcomes, and a bet as a bet of at most 10 points (a random part of a bet is a smaller bet).

## Data risk classification

Sherlock is approved for computing with Low and Moderate Risk data only.
Sherlock is not approved to store or process HIPAA, PHI, PII nor any
kind of High Risk data. See
https://www.sherlock.stanford.edu/docs/concepts/ for details.

Before inspecting a project that may hold data above those levels, such as
health records, identifiable human subject data, or export-controlled material,
stop and ask for the data's risk classification and a non-sensitive description
only; do not request records or inspect more of the data. If the classification
stays unclear, stop and refer the user to Stanford Research Computing
(srcc-support@stanford.edu). If the data is above the approved level, stop work
in that project and direct the user to Stanford Research Computing
(srcc-support@stanford.edu).

## Sanctions

termination of the user's account on the first occurrence. Unauthorized access
mechanisms, credential collection or sharing, and bypassing controls result in
immediate termination of the user's account and referral to Stanford information
security. Running an SSH server, on any node and in any form (see Access
controls in /etc/agents/AGENTS.md), can lead to the suspension of the user's
account.

## Prohibited mechanisms

This expands on the Access controls in /etc/agents/AGENTS.md, without
limitation: tunnels left running unattended, stored MFA secrets,
web shells, background agents that accept external commands, and hiding
processes from the user or from `ps`. A user's request does not authorize any of
these, regardless of the reason given.

## Unattended agent sessions

A session that runs a bounded task to completion while the user is away is
fine: waiting for a job to finish, fixing what failed and resubmitting, then
stopping, all within the user's own allocations and files. The user remains
accountable for every action their tools take, including actions taken while
they are away. What is not allowed: supervisors, watchdogs, cron-like loops or
scripts that keep agent sessions alive, restart them or feed them new prompts
when nobody is there; sessions designed to run indefinitely or to be picked up
day after day without a person in the loop; and on a login node, the Login
nodes rule in /etc/agents/AGENTS.md applies in full, session open or not. A
request to
build such a setup is refused like any other conflicting request (see

rule in /etc/agents/AGENTS.md and get terminated; that is not a system fault to
report. Stop Slurm jobs with
`scancel`, never by killing processes on a compute node directly (see
Authorized access only in
/etc/agents/AGENTS.md). If you suspect a problem with the system itself rather
than with a job or process you own, stop and tell the user (see Support in
/etc/agents/AGENTS.md). A draft report for them includes the hostname, time,
job ID and path involved, never sensitive data.

## Agent-specific notes

approve running each command outside the sandbox. That is expected

"""RSA pragmatic listener at depth 2 with singleton salience, contextual distinctiveness, visual feature complexity, evaluative valence framing, visual color contrast, and literal L0.

Refining rsa_l2_singleton_distinct_feat_color_l0 by incorporating the evaluative valence framing component from polarity_congruence_listener:
speakers and listeners reason at depth 2 (inverting a speaker who simulates a depth-1 pragmatic listener) with
common knowledge of an object prior combining discrete visual singleton salience (favoring unique objects with
no duplicates in the scene), continuous contextual distinctiveness (favoring objects with greater feature contrast
relative to the rest of the display), visual feature complexity modulated by evaluative framing valence (favoring
feature-rich items under neutral/positive framing but inverting to favor sparse, featureless items when referring
to a least favorite object), and visual color contrast (favoring fully colored objects over desaturated grayscale
distractors). Crucially, the foundational simulated literal listener L0 operates purely on truth-conditional semantics
without perceptual bias, preventing redundant prior compounding across reasoning tiers. On prior trials with no
informative word, choices are governed directly by the combined perceptual prior. A lapse parameter mixes in uniform guessing.
"""

import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpyro.distributions as dist
from memo import memo

from src.rsa.memo_kit import EPS, at, softmax_prior, vec, with_lapse

PARAMS = {
    "alpha": dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_singleton": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_distinct": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_features": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_valence": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_color": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
}


@memo
def L0[u: UTT, r: OBJ](lex: ...):
    listener: knows(u)
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=at(lex, u, r))
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


@memo
def L1[u: UTT, r: OBJ](alpha, lex: ..., prior: ...):
    listener: thinks[
        speaker: given(r in OBJ, wpp=vec(prior, r)),
        speaker: chooses(
            u in UTT,
            wpp=at(lex, u, r)
            * exp(alpha * log(L0[u, r](lex) + {EPS})),
        ),
    ]
    listener: observes [speaker.u] is u
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=Pr[speaker.r == r])
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


@memo
def L2[u: UTT, r: OBJ](alpha, lex: ..., prior: ...):
    listener: thinks[
        speaker: given(r in OBJ, wpp=vec(prior, r)),
        speaker: chooses(
            u in UTT,
            wpp=at(lex, u, r)
            * exp(alpha * log(L1[u, r](alpha, lex, prior) + {EPS})),
        ),
    ]
    listener: observes [speaker.u] is u
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=Pr[speaker.r == r])
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


def listener(params, ctx):
    diffs = jnp.abs(ctx.lex[:, :, None] - ctx.lex[:, None, :])
    pair_dist = jnp.sum(diffs * (1.0 - ctx.is_sink[:, None, None]), axis=0)
    gray_diff = jnp.abs(ctx.grayscale[:, None] - ctx.grayscale[None, :])
    fam_diff = jnp.abs(
        ctx.familiarization[:, None] - ctx.familiarization[None, :]
    )
    total_dist = pair_dist + gray_diff + fam_diff
    duplicate_count = jnp.sum(total_dist == 0, axis=1)
    is_singleton = jnp.where(duplicate_count == 1, 1.0, 0.0)

    real_lex = ctx.lex * (1.0 - ctx.is_sink[:, None])
    diff = jnp.abs(real_lex[:, :, None] - real_lex[:, None, :])
    distinct = jnp.sum(diff, axis=(0, 2))

    effective_w_features = (
        params["w_features"] + ctx.valence * params["w_valence"]
    )

    prior = softmax_prior(
        params["w_singleton"] * is_singleton
        + params["w_distinct"] * distinct
        + effective_w_features * ctx.feature_count
        + params["w_color"] * (1.0 - ctx.grayscale)
    )

    heard = L2(params["alpha"], ctx.lex, prior)[ctx.utterance]
    return jnp.where(ctx.is_prior > 0, prior, heard)

<content>
1: """A frozen paradigm and its design -> what each participant sees, and the data back
2: (docs/auto_open/PLAN.md §4: the page, the pilot and the data all come from these lists).
3: 
4: The plan had an implementer agent write each paradigm's jsPsych page. Every spec uses one of
5: six response widgets with SVG or text materials, so the page is instead one generic, tested
6: player (`src/rsa_open/page.html`, `src.rsa_open.page`) of the lists built here, and the
7: simulated pilot (`src.rsa_open.pilot`) reads the same lists: what LLM participants see is
8: what people see.
9: 
10: **Trial lists** (`trial_lists`): one list per participant, a pure function of (paradigm, design,
11: seed, list index), so randomisation happens here, not in the page:
12: - **test trials**: the design's units (`src.rsa_open.design`: a scene and, by response type, a
13:   probed object, a target, a judged message). List ``p`` takes ``trials_per_participant``
14:   consecutive units of one shuffled order of the design, starting at ``p x trials``, so every
15:   unit is answered equally often (to within one) across lists; the list shuffles them.
16: - **catch trials** (``design.catch_trials``) at random positions, and one **practice** trial
17:   first: a scene with a word true of exactly one object (the closed campaign's
18:   `_catch_spec`), each with what passing means (`CATCH_RULES`). A judgment's catch trials
19:   alternate that word for its object (answer yes) and for another object, of which it is false
20:   (answer no), so answering one way fails.
21: - **domains** rotate (least used first, not the previous trial's when another can serve), and
22:   each trial maps the scene's abstract features onto distinct features of its domain at random;
23:   the objects' screen order is a random permutation (``display_order[p]`` is the scene's object

"""A frozen paradigm and its design -> what each participant sees, and the data back
(docs/auto_open/PLAN.md §4: the page, the pilot and the data all come from these lists).

The plan had an implementer agent write each paradigm's jsPsych page. Every spec uses one of
six response widgets with SVG or text materials, so the page is instead one generic, tested
player (`src/rsa_open/page.html`, `src.rsa_open.page`) of the lists built here, and the
simulated pilot (`src.rsa_open.pilot`) reads the same lists: what LLM participants see is
what people see.

**Trial lists** (`trial_lists`): one list per participant, a pure function of (paradigm, design,
seed, list index), so randomisation happens here, not in the page:
- **test trials**: the design's units (`src.rsa_open.design`: a scene and, by response type, a
  probed object, a target, a judged message). List ``p`` takes ``trials_per_participant``
  consecutive units of one shuffled order of the design, starting at ``p x trials``, so every
  unit is answered equally often (to within one) across lists; the list shuffles them.
- **catch trials** (``design.catch_trials``) at random positions, and one **practice** trial
  first: a scene with a word true of exactly one object (the closed campaign's
  `_catch_spec`), each with what passing means (`CATCH_RULES`). A judgment's catch trials
  alternate that word for its object (answer yes) and for another object, of which it is false
  (answer no), so answering one way fails.
- **domains** rotate (least used first, not the previous trial's when another can serve), and
  each trial maps the scene's abstract features onto distinct features of its domain at random;
  the objects' screen order is a random permutation (``display_order[p]`` is the scene's object
  at screen position ``p``).
- **rendering**: each object is drawn as an SVG (the domain's base, then its features' fragments,
  in a 100 x 100 box) or written as a phrase ("a house with a garden and with a pool"); the
  prompt shows the message as the speaker's word. A production trial's buttons are the scene's
  words in a random order; a slider or rating names its ends.

**Data**: the page records, per trial, the trial's scene, its list fields and ``response``
in the link's form (`src.rsa_open.links.LinkLikelihood.encode`), with objects and messages as
scene indices, never screen positions. `scenes_and_responses` turns test rows back into scenes
(the design pool's abstract feature names, as the theories saw in design) and responses, and
`catch_passed` scores a catch trial.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import html
import json
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

import numpy as np

from src.rsa.context import Context
from src.rsa.design_space import feature_names as abstract_feature_names

SCHEMA = "rsa_open_lists/1"
PRACTICE_SHAPE = (3, 2)
SUBSET_STREAM = 2**31 - 1
UNIT_FIELDS = ("probe", "target", "utterance")
PHASES = ("practice", "test", "catch")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- the design

def design_units(report: Mapping[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """The design's units from an EIG report (`src.rsa_open.design.score_paradigm`)."""
    units = []
    for i, u in enumerate(report["design"]):
        unit = {"objects": [list(map(int, row)) for row in u["objects"]], "heard": u["heard"],
                **{k: int(u[k]) for k in UNIT_FIELDS if k in u}}
        scene_of(unit)  # a unit that is not a valid scene fails here
        units.append(unit)
    if not units:
        raise ValueError("the design has no units")
    return units


def design_sha256(units: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> str:
    blob = json.dumps(list(units), sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
    return hashlib.sha256(blob.encode()).hexdigest()


def scene_of(trial: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Context:
    """The abstract scene of a unit or trial: the design pool's feature names."""
    objects = tuple(tuple(int(v) for v in row) for row in trial["objects"])
    return Context(objects=objects, feature_names=abstract_feature_names(len(objects[0])),
                   utterance=trial["heard"])


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- catch trials

def _catch(shape: Tuple[int, int], rng: np.random.Generator, response_type: str, k: int,
           options: Mapping[str, int]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """An unambiguous trial and what passing it means, for the ``k``-th catch trial."""
    from src.rsa.experiment.design import _catch_spec

    spec, target = _catch_spec(shape, rng)
    word = spec.utterance
    objects = [list(r) for r in spec.objects]
    trial: Dict[str, Any] = {"objects": objects, "heard": word}
    if response_type == "choice":
        trial["expect"] = {"choice": target}
    elif response_type == "rating":
        points = options["scale_points"]
        trial.update(probe=target, expect={"min_rating": (points + 1) // 2 + 1})
    elif response_type == "slider":
        top = options["total_points"]
        trial.update(probe=target, expect={"min_value": top // 2 + 1})
    elif response_type == "bet":
        top = options["total_points"]
        trial["expect"] = {"object": target, "min_points": top // 2 + 1}
    elif response_type == "production":
        true_words = [f for f, v in enumerate(spec.objects[target]) if v]
        trial.update(target=target, expect={"utterance_in": true_words})
    elif response_type == "binary_judgment":
        if k % 2 == 1:  # the word is false of every other object
            others = [i for i in range(len(objects)) if i != target]
            trial.update(target=others[int(rng.integers(len(others)))], utterance=word, expect={"answer": False})
        else:
            trial.update(target=target, utterance=word, expect={"answer": True})
    else:
        raise KeyError(response_type)
    return trial


def catch_passed(row: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
    """Whether a catch or practice trial's response meets its rule."""

display.text:
"""The RSA live campaign's launcher config: check it, show its cost, render Prolific's settings.

    uv run python -m src.rsa.live.config --config scripts/rsa/live/rsa_live.yaml --check
    uv run python -m src.rsa.live.config --config scripts/rsa/live/rsa_live.yaml --render   # into this checkout

``--check`` validates the config and prints what a launch would recruit and
cost (Prolific's reward plus its service fee, main's estimate). ``--render``
writes the ``prolific:`` block to the RSA project's ``prolific_config.yaml``
(gitignored; main's deployment reads it), without a participant count: the
count reaches the pipeline once, as ``--participants``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List

import tyro
import yaml

from src.pipelines.outer_loop.deployment.prolific import build_eligibility_filters, compute_reward_cents
from src.rsa.live.collect import PROJECT_ID
from src.runtime.prolific import prolific_config_path

PROLIFIC_SERVICE_FEE = 0.33  # main's estimate (scripts/outer_loop_live/_pilot_config.py); check the account's rate
REQUIRED = ("firebase_project", "series_label", "chains", "experiments", "participants", "trials", "displays",
            "prolific")


@dataclass
class Args:
    config: Path
    check: bool = False
    render: bool = False
    launch_experiments: int = 0
    """With ``array``: print what a launch of experiments 1..N on those array tasks publishes."""
    array: str = ""
    """Slurm array spec of the launch (e.g. "0-2", "0", "0,2")."""


def load(path: Path) -> dict:
    cfg = yaml.safe_load(Path(path).read_text())
    missing = [k for k in REQUIRED if k not in cfg]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"{path} lacks {missing}")
    if "participants" in cfg["prolific"] or "total_available_places" in cfg["prolific"]:
        raise ValueError("the participant count is the top-level `participants`, not a prolific: key")
    if not isinstance(cfg.get("confirm_live_recruitment", False), bool):
        raise ValueError("confirm_live_recruitment must be true or false")
    for k in cfg["chains"]:
        site = hosting_site(cfg, k)
        if len(site) > 30 or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9-]+", site):
            raise ValueError(f"Hosting site id {site!r} must be <= 30 characters of [a-z0-9-]")
    build_eligibility_filters(cfg["prolific"])  # raises on a bad approval rate
    minutes = cfg["prolific"].get("estimated_completion_time")
    if not isinstance(minutes, int) or minutes < 1:
        # Prolific takes whole minutes, and main's deploy truncates (int(2.5) = 2): the pilot's
        # report caught a 2.5 that would have been listed as 2 (PILOT_REPORT.md §6).
        raise ValueError(f"estimated_completion_time must be whole minutes, not {minutes!r}")
    trials, displays = cfg["trials"], cfg["displays"]
    if not (isinstance(trials, int) and isinstance(displays, int) and 1 <= trials <= displays):
        raise ValueError(f"trials ({trials!r}) must be whole and between 1 and displays ({displays!r})")
    if (cfg["participants"] * trials) % displays:
        raise ValueError(f"{cfg['participants']} people x {trials} trials do not spread evenly over {displays} displays")
    return cfg


def hosting_site(cfg: dict, chain: int) -> str:
    return f"{cfg['firebase_project']}-{cfg['series_label']}-c{chain}"


def cost(cfg: dict) -> dict:
    reward = compute_reward_cents(cfg["prolific"])
    per_study = reward * cfg["participants"]
    per_study_total = per_study + round(per_study * PROLIFIC_SERVICE_FEE)
    studies = len(cfg["chains"]) * cfg["experiments"]
    return dict(reward_cents=reward, per_study_cents=per_study_total, studies=studies,
                participants=studies * cfg["participants"], total_cents=per_study_total * studies)


def render(cfg: dict) -> Path:
    path = prolific_config_path(PROJECT_ID)
    if not path.parent.is_dir():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no project directory {path.parent}")
    header = "# AUTO-GENERATED by `python -m src.rsa.live.config --render` from the RSA live config. Do not edit.\n\n"
    path.write_text(header + yaml.safe_dump(cfg["prolific"], sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True), encoding="utf-8")
    return path


def summary(cfg: dict) -> List[str]:
    c = cost(cfg)
    return [
        f"study name     : {cfg['prolific']['name']}",
        f"chains         : {cfg['chains']}  (sites {', '.join(hosting_site(cfg, k) for k in cfg['chains'])})",
        f"per experiment : {cfg['participants']} people x {cfg['trials']} of {cfg['displays']} displays "
        f"(+ catch), {cfg['prolific']['estimated_completion_time']} min, "
        f"reward ${c['reward_cents'] / 100:.2f} each; ${c['per_study_cents'] / 100:,.2f} with the fee",
        f"campaign       : {c['studies']} studies, {c['participants']} people, ~${c['total_cents'] / 100:,.2f}",
        f"confirmed      : {cfg.get('confirm_live_recruitment', False)}",
    ]


def array_tasks(spec: str) -> List[int]:
    """Slurm array indices: "0-2" -> [0, 1, 2], "0,2" -> [0, 2]."""
    tasks: List[int] = []
    for part in spec.split(","):
        lo, _, hi = part.strip().partition("-")
        if not lo.isdigit() or (hi and not hi.isdigit()):
            raise ValueError(f"array spec {spec!r} is not like 0-2 or 0,2")
        tasks += list(range(int(lo), int(hi or lo) + 1))
    return sorted(set(tasks))


def launch_summary(cfg: dict, n_experiments: int, array: str) -> str:
    """What a launch of experiments 1..n_experiments on ``array``'s chains publishes
    at most (finished experiments are not rerun: a resumed chain publishes fewer)."""
    chains = len(array_tasks(array))
    studies = chains * n_experiments
    return (f"this launch    : experiments 1-{n_experiments} of {chains} chain(s): up to {studies} studies, "
            f"~${studies * cost(cfg)['per_study_cents'] / 100:,.2f} (finished experiments are not rerun)")


def main(args: Args) -> None:
    cfg = load(args.config)
    if args.check:
        print("\n".join(summary(cfg)), file=sys.stderr)
    if args.launch_experiments:
        print(launch_summary(cfg, args.launch_experiments, args.array), file=sys.stderr)
    if args.render:
        print(f"[render] wrote {render(cfg)}", file=sys.stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(tyro.cli(Args))

Main's machinery does the deployment and the recruiting
(`src.pipelines.outer_loop.deployment.local.run_deployment`; `collect.py`'s

reference game:

* the page (`src.rsa.live.site`): server-assigned lists, a post to /submit;

* participant ids: ``live<k>``, numbered across the run's experiments, from a

  ids, go to the private directory, never to the run tree the agents read.

Every failure raises: a study that ran must never read as "nobody responded".
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import urllib.request
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

import pandas as pd

from src.pipelines.outer_loop.collect import (
    _PROLIFIC_MAX_WAIT_SEC,
    _pause_unfilled_study,
    _poll_prolific_until_target,
    _results_request,
)
from src.pipelines.outer_loop.deployment.manifest import manifest_path, recorded_live_study
from src.rsa.experiment.convert import convert
from src.rsa.live.site import build_live_site

PROJECT_ID = "rsa_reference"  # the Prolific config's project (src/pipelines/outer_loop/projects/)


TRIALS_FORMAT = "rsa_jspsych_json"  # how the page stores its data in Firestore (src.rsa.live.site)


def decode_trials(stored) -> List[dict]:
    """The page's jsPsych records from a stored response's ``trials``: one
    JSON string (Firestore rejects nested arrays, and each trial's display is
    a matrix). Anything else is not this page's data, and raises."""
    if (isinstance(stored, list) and len(stored) == 1 and isinstance(stored[0], dict)
            and stored[0].get("format") == TRIALS_FORMAT and isinstance(stored[0].get("data"), str)):
        records = json.loads(stored[0]["data"])
        if not isinstance(records, list):
            raise ValueError("the stored jsPsych data are not a list of records")
        return records
    raise ValueError(f"stored trials are not {TRIALS_FORMAT!r} (one JSON string): another page's data?")


class DraftOnly(RuntimeError):
    """A test-mode deployment: the page is live and the study is a Prolific draft, nothing to collect."""


@dataclass
class LiveSettings:
    prolific_mode: str  # "test" (a draft to preview) or "live" (published; real money)
    firebase_project: Optional[str]
    run_label: str  # this run's label on its Hosting site and study (e.g. "c0")

    """The experiment's deployment manifest: the recorded live study if there is
    one (a resumed run never deploys or publishes twice), else a new deployment."""
    from src.pipelines.outer_loop.deployment.local import run_deployment

    if s.prolific_mode not in ("test", "live"):

        if len(lists_doc["lists"]) != n_participants:
            raise ValueError(f"{len(lists_doc['lists'])} trial lists for {n_participants} participants")
        build_live_site(lists_doc, exp_dir, overwrite=True)
        run_deployment(exp_dir=exp_dir, project_id=PROJECT_ID, run_id=experiment, deploy_target="firebase",
                       prolific_mode=s.prolific_mode, agent_backend="opencode", collection_owner=s.collection_owner,
                       firebase_project=s.firebase_project, firebase_region=s.firebase_region,
                       n_participants=n_participants, repo_root=s.repo_root, run_label=s.run_label)
    manifest = json.loads(manifest_path(exp_dir).read_text())
    if s.prolific_mode == "test":
        raise DraftOnly(f"test mode: the page is at {manifest.get('experiment_url')} and Prolific study "
                        f"{manifest.get('prolific_study_id')} is a draft to preview; nothing to collect")
    return manifest


def wait_for_participants(manifest: dict, target: int, log_dir: Path, max_wait_sec: float) -> int:
    """Poll Prolific until ``target`` submissions or the wait ends; pause a study left short."""
    study = manifest.get("prolific_study_id")
    if not study:
        raise RuntimeError("the deployment recorded no Prolific study: nothing to collect from")
    completed = _poll_prolific_until_target(study, target, log_dir, max_wait_sec=max_wait_sec)
    if completed < target:
        _pause_unfilled_study(study, completed, target, log_dir)
    return completed


def fetch_responses(manifest: dict) -> List[dict]:
    """Every stored response of the deployment's collection session, whole."""
    base = manifest.get("results_api_url")
    session = manifest.get("collection_session_id")
    if not base or not session:
        raise RuntimeError("the deployment manifest has no results_api_url or collection_session_id")
    url = f"{base.rstrip('/')}/results?collection_session_id={session}&format=json"
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(_results_request(url), timeout=120) as r:
            body = json.loads(r.read().decode("utf-8"))
    except Exception as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(f"live results fetch failed for {url}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}. The participants' "
                           "data are on the server: refusing to report zero responses.") from exc
    if not isinstance(body, list):
        raise RuntimeError(f"{url} returned {type(body).__name__}, not a list of responses")
    return body


def responses_to_rows(responses: List[dict], *, study_id: str, experiment: str,
                      ids: Dict[str, str]) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, Dict[str, str], dict]:
    """Canonical rows for the study's responses. ``ids`` maps Prolific ids to the
    run's participant ids (extended here: new people get the next ``live<k>``).
    Responses of another study (a preview, a test submission) are left out, on record."""
    ids = dict(ids)
    frames, other, empty = [], [], []
    for resp in sorted(responses, key=lambda r: (r.get("submitted_at_client") or "", r["participant_id_str"])):
        if resp.get("prolific_study_id") != study_id:
            other.append(resp["participant_id_str"])
            continue
        pid = resp.get("prolific_pid") or resp["participant_id_str"]
        if pid not in ids:
            ids[pid] = f"live{len(ids)}"
        frame = convert(decode_trials(resp["trials"]), participant_id=ids[pid], experiment=experiment)
        if frame.empty:
            empty.append(ids[pid])
            continue
        frames.append(frame)
    if not frames:
        raise RuntimeError(f"no response of study {study_id} has any trial ({len(responses)} responses stored)")
    record = dict(n_responses=len(frames), other_study=len(other), without_trials=empty)
    return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True), ids, record

166:                             for k, item in enumerate(history))
167:     else:
168:         earlier = "- None: this is the chain's first experiment."
169:     tool = f"{TOOLS_COMMAND} {{command}} --workspace {ws.root} --spec {ws.work}/<your spec>.json"
170:     return f"""# You design the next experiment
171: 
172: You are the experiment designer of chain `{chain}`, experiment {experiment}, in a study of how
173: people interpret and choose referring expressions. Theories of this ability are judged by how well
174: they predict people **across paradigms**: a theory fitted to one task can be overfit to that task
175: (Yarkoni, 2020, "The generalizability crisis"). Your job: design the experiment that matters most
176: for arriving at theories that generalize, given the earlier paradigms in this chain and the
177: current theories. You choose the task, the materials, the instructions and the response (any of
178: the library's response types); nothing requires your paradigm to resemble or differ from earlier
179: ones. Decide what is most important to learn next, and say why.
180: 
181: ## The charter (every paradigm must fit it)
182: 
183: {CHARTER}
184: 
185: ## What a paradigm is
186: 
187: A paradigm is one JSON spec: schema `{ws.inputs / 'paradigm_schema.json'}`, a format example (placeholder
188: content only) `{ws.inputs / 'format_example.json'}`. Every trial is an abstract scene: a few objects
189: (rows) with binary features (columns); each feature is a word the speaker can say. Your domains
190: give each feature its word and its drawing (an SVG fragment in a 100 x 100 box, drawn over the
191: domain's base) or its phrase (text materials). The response types and the links that score them:
192: `{ws.inputs / 'links.md'}`. The theories are written over abstract scenes and never see your
193: words or drawings; your materials decide whether people perceive the scene the theories assume.
194: The page shows the speaker's word in quotation marks where your prompt says `{{message}}`: do not
195: add your own.
196: 
197: **Materials people can read, and want to look at.** Scenes include objects with no features, and
198: objects with every feature, so:
199: - the base must be a complete, recognisable object on its own (a robot with a face and a body,
200:   not a bare box): it is what an object with no features looks like;
201: - each feature is a separate, nameable part, clearly visible at card size (about 180 px), that does
202:   not look like part of the base or like another feature, and that can be added to the base
203:   alongside any other features without hiding them;
204: - each word is a common, concrete word that a person would use for that part of the drawing;
205: - make them engaging: colour and a little character, nothing cluttered or abstract.
206: The pilot checks this (see "After you submit"): fresh participants name each domain's base in
207: their own words (no options to choose from), say which of your words names the part each single
208: feature adds, and say exactly which objects of real trial screens a word is true of.
209: 
210: The harness builds the page from your spec: one list per participant (balanced over your design),
211: a practice trial, your comprehension checks (shown again once after a wrong answer), catch trials
212: with one right answer, objects in a random screen order, words mapped to features at random per
213: trial. You write no page code.
214: 
215: ## The current theories
216: 
217: Their files (read-only) are in `{ws.context / 'theories'}`, their posterior draws on the data so far in
218: `{ws.context / 'draws'}`.
219: {theories}
220: 
221: ## Earlier paradigms in this chain
222: 
223: {earlier}
224: 
225: ## Bounds
226: 
227: - Budget: ${BUDGET_USD:.2f} per experiment (participants x pay x 4/3, Prolific's fee). At least
228:   {MIN_PARTICIPANTS} participants, at most {MAX_MINUTES} minutes each, at least ${MIN_HOURLY_USD:.2f} per hour.
229: - Scenes: 2-{MAX_OBJECTS} objects, 2-{MAX_FEATURES} features, at most {MAX_POOL} scenes in the space.
230: - Content (IRB): no deception, no affectively charged stimuli or language, SVG or text materials
231:   only, no links or requests for personal information.
232: 
233: ## Your tools ({calls_left} calls left; each command is one call)
234: 
235:     {tool.format(command="validate")}     # every problem with the spec, at once; the time estimate
236:     {tool.format(command="eig")}          # bits per dollar under the theories, the floor; the time estimate
237:     {tool.format(command="eig")} --quick  # the same, approximate, in a fraction of the time: for exploring
238:     {tool.format(command="link-check")}   # can the link's parameters be recovered in this paradigm?
239:     {tool.format(command="submit")}       # submit (needs a passing eig and link-check of this exact spec)
240: 
241: - Give the shell tool a timeout of {TOOL_SHELL_TIMEOUT_MS} ms for `eig` and `link-check`: `eig` takes
242:   5-15 minutes, `link-check` fits three models (5-20 minutes). With the default timeout they are
243:   killed before they print anything. Compare candidate paradigms with `eig --quick` (1-2
244:   minutes) and run the full `eig` on the one you mean to submit.
245: - `link-check` simulates from the live theory with the most parameters; `--theory <name>` names
246:   another. A theory that cannot move a link parameter (the literal listener is flat over the
247:   objects a word is true of, so a listener link's temperature changes nothing) cannot recover it.
248: - **Time:** how long people took in finished experiments, and how many trials fit in a minute:
249:   `{ws.inputs / 'timing.md'}`. `validate` and `eig` report the pilot's time estimate for your spec
250:   against your declared minutes; the pilot's check uses the same estimate.
251: - **The floor:** `eig` reports your paradigm's expected information gain about the theories per
252:   dollar; `submit` needs at least {FLOOR_SHARE:.0%} of what the closed campaign's forced-choice
253:   paradigm gives under the same theories.
254: - Every report is saved in `{ws.reports}`. Keep notes in `{ws.work}/notes.md`: a later session of this
255:   cycle starts with no memory but your files.
256: 
257: ## After you submit
258: 
259: The harness re-scores your spec with its own seed (the design that runs is its), re-checks the
260: link, builds the page and pilots it with LLM participants. The pilot passes when at least
261: {FLOORS['comprehension']:.0%} of them understand the instructions (by their second reading), at least
262: {FLOORS['catch']:.0%} of catch trials are passed, {FLOORS['readable']:.0%} of answers are usable, the data parse, its
263: time estimate is within {TIME_TOLERANCE:.0%} of your declared minutes, and (SVG materials) at least {FLOORS['legibility']:.0%} of
264: its materials questions are answered right, with no feature or trial screen misread by half of them (a base
265: named otherwise counts against that rate). If anything fails you get the report
266: and may revise: {submissions_left} submission(s) left in this cycle, about {seconds_left // 60} minutes of your time.
267: 
268: ## What to write
269: 
270: 1. Your spec(s) in `{ws.work}`; submit one.
271: 2. `{ws.work}/rationale.md`: what this experiment is for, which disagreements among the theories it
272:    targets, why this task and response type, and what you expect each theory to predict.
273: 
274: You have no internet access. Work only in `{ws.work}`.
275: {feedback}"""
276: 
277: 
278: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- the harness's checks
279: 
280: @dataclass
281: class SubmissionResult:
282:     sha256: str
283:     passed: bool
284:     problems: List[str]
285:     dir: Path
286:     details: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
287: 
288:     def feedback(self) -> str:
289:         lines = [f"Submission {self.sha256[:12]} did not pass:"] + [f"- {p}" for p in self.problems]
290:         return "\n".join(lines)
291: 
292: 
293: def check_submission(ws: Workspace, submitted: Path, out: Path, *, pilot_participants: int,
294:                      participant_factory=None) -> SubmissionResult:
295:     """The harness's own checks of a submission record (validation, floor, link, pilot)."""
296:     from src.rsa_open.paradigm import ParadigmInvalid, load_paradigm
297:     from src.rsa_open.pilot import run_pilot
298:     from src.rsa_open.screens import design_units, trial_lists
299:     from src.rsa_open.tools import eig_report, link_check_report
300: 
301:     record = json.loads(Path(submitted).read_text())
302:     out.mkdir(parents=True)
303:     spec = out / "paradigm.json"
304:     shutil.copyfile(record["spec"], spec)
305:     sha = record["sha256"]
306:     try:
307:         paradigm = load_paradigm(spec)
308:     except ParadigmInvalid as err:
309:         return SubmissionResult(sha, False, [f"the spec is not valid: {err}"], out)
310:     if paradigm.sha256 != sha:
311:         return SubmissionResult(sha, False, ["the spec changed after it was submitted (its sha256 differs)"], out)
312:     eig = eig_report(ws, spec, seed=seed_for(sha, "harness_eig"))
313:     (out / "eig.json").write_text(json.dumps(eig, indent=2))
314:     if not eig["meets_floor"]:
315:         return SubmissionResult(sha, False, [
316:             f"below the floor on the harness's re-score: {eig['bits_per_dollar']:.5f} bits/$ against "
317:             f"{eig['floor_bits_per_dollar']:.5f}"], out, {"eig": eig})
318:     link = link_check_report(ws, spec, seed=seed_for(sha, "harness_link_check"))
319:     (out / "link_check.json").write_text(json.dumps(link, indent=2))
320:     if not (link["converged"] and link["recovered"]):
321:         return SubmissionResult(sha, False, [
322:             f"the link check failed on the harness's re-run: converged={link['converged']}, "
323:             f"misses={link['misses']}"], out, {"eig": eig, "link": link})
324:     units = design_units(eig)
325:     lists = trial_lists(paradigm, units, seed=seed_for(sha, "lists"))
326:     (out / "lists.json").write_text(json.dumps(lists))
327:     pilot = run_pilot(paradigm, lists, out / "pilot", n_participants=pilot_participants,
328:                       participant_factory=participant_factory, timing=ws.timing_records())
329:     if not pilot["passed"]:
330:         return SubmissionResult(sha, False, [f"pilot: {p}" for p in pilot["problems"]], out,
331:                                 {"eig": eig, "link": link, "pilot": pilot})
332:     return SubmissionResult(sha, True, [], out, {"eig": eig, "link": link, "pilot": pilot, "lists": lists,
333:                                                  "paradigm": paradigm, "units": units})
334: 
335: 
336: def _sha_file(path: Path) -> str:
337:     return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
338: 
339: 
340: def freeze(result: SubmissionResult, out: Path, *, chain: str, experiment: int,
341:            code_commit: Optional[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
342:     """Write the paradigm that passed, and its record, to ``out`` (once)."""
343:     from src.rsa_open.page import render
344:     from src.rsa_open.screens import design_sha256
345: 
346:     if out.exists():
347:         raise FileExistsError(f"{out} exists: a paradigm is frozen once")
348:     out.mkdir(parents=True)
349:     d = result.details
350:     paradigm = d["paradigm"]
351:     (out / "paradigm.json").write_text(json.dumps(paradigm.model_dump(mode="json"), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
352:     (out / "design.json").write_text(json.dumps({"units": d["units"], "eig": d["eig"]}, indent=2))
353:     (out / "lists.json").write_text(json.dumps(d["lists"]))
354:     (out / "page_preview.html").write_text(render(d["lists"], preview=True))
355:     (out / "link_check.json").write_text(json.dumps(d["link"], indent=2))
356:     shutil.copytree(result.dir / "pilot", out / "pilot")
357:     record = {
358:         "chain": chain, "experiment": experiment, "paradigm_sha256": paradigm.sha256,
359:         "design_sha256": design_sha256(d["units"]), "lists_sha256": _sha_file(out / "lists.json"),
360:         "context_sha256": d["eig"]["context_sha256"], "joint_eig_bits": d["eig"]["joint_eig_bits"],
361:         "bits_per_dollar": d["eig"]["bits_per_dollar"], "floor_bits_per_dollar": d["eig"]["floor_bits_per_dollar"],
362:         "pilot": {k: d["pilot"][k] for k in ("comprehension_final", "catch_pass", "readable", "estimated_minutes",
363:                                              "participant_model")},
364:         "review_required": experiment == 1, "frozen_at": time.time(), "code_commit": code_commit,
365:     }
366:     (out / "record.json").write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2))
367:     return record
368: 
369: 
370: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- a cycle, and the retry
371: 
372: def run_designer(root: Path, *, chain: str, experiment: int,
373:                  theories: Mapping[str, Tuple[Path, Mapping[str, np.ndarray]]], hypotheses: Mapping[str, str],
374:                  history: Sequence[EarlierParadigm], spawn: SpawnFn, pilot_participants: int = 12,
375:                  participant_factory=None, code_commit: Optional[str] = None,
376:                  cycle_seconds: int = CYCLE_SECONDS,
377:                  timing: Sequence[TimingRecord] = CLOSED_CAMPAIGN) -> Dict[str, Any]:
378:     """Design one experiment: up to ``MAX_CYCLES`` cycles; returns the frozen record. ``timing``
379:     is every finished experiment's completion times (`src.rsa_open.timing`): the closed
380:     campaign's, plus this campaign's from every chain."""
381:     root = Path(root)
382:     failures: List[str] = []
383:     for cycle in range(MAX_CYCLES):
384:         ws = prepare_workspace(root / f"cycle_{cycle + 1}", theories=theories, history=history, timing=timing)
385:         feedback = ""
386:         if failures:
387:             feedback = ("\n## The previous attempt failed\n\nA previous designer cycle for this experiment "
388:                         f"failed: {failures[-1]}\nThis is the last attempt.\n")
389:         spent, failed_shas = 0.0, set()
390:         reason = None
391:         for k in range(MAX_SUBMISSIONS):
392:             left = int(cycle_seconds - spent)
393:             if left < MIN_SESSION_SECONDS:
394:                 reason = "the designer's time for the cycle was spent without a passing submission"
395:                 break
396:             if len(ws.calls()) >= MAX_TOOL_CALLS:
397:                 reason = "the designer's tool calls for the cycle were spent without a passing submission"
398:                 break
399:             prompt = brief(ws, chain=chain, experiment=experiment, hypotheses=hypotheses, history=history,
400:                            feedback=feedback, submissions_left=MAX_SUBMISSIONS - k, seconds_left=left)
401:             (ws.root / "logs" / f"brief_{k + 1}.md").write_text(prompt)
402:             started = time.monotonic()
403:             ok = spawn(ws, prompt, left, ws.root / "logs" / f"agent_{k + 1}.jsonl")
404:             took = time.monotonic() - started
405:             spent += took
406:             if not ws.submission.exists():
407:                 if took >= left - 5:
408:                     reason = (f"the designer's session reached its time limit ({left // 60} min) without a "
409:                               f"submission")
410:                 elif not ok:
411:                     reason = "the designer's session failed (the agent exited with an error) without a submission"
412:                 else:
413:                     reason = "the designer's session ended without a submission"
414:                 break
415:             submitted = ws.root / "submissions" / f"{k + 1}.json"
416:             submitted.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
417:             os.replace(ws.submission, submitted)  # the next session must submit anew
418:             sha = json.loads(submitted.read_text())["sha256"]
419:             if sha in failed_shas:
420:                 result = SubmissionResult(sha, False, ["this exact spec already failed; it was not checked again"],
421:                                           ws.root / "checks" / f"{k + 1}")
422:             else:
423:                 result = check_submission(ws, submitted, ws.root / "checks" / f"{k + 1}",
424:                                           pilot_participants=pilot_participants,
425:                                           participant_factory=participant_factory)
426:             if result.passed:
427:                 return freeze(result, root / "frozen", chain=chain, experiment=experiment, code_commit=code_commit)
428:             failed_shas.add(sha)
429:             where = f" Its reports (and the pilot's transcripts) are in `{result.dir}`." if result.dir.exists() else ""
430:             feedback = (f"\n## Your last submission did not pass\n\n{result.feedback()}\n\n"
431:                         f"Revise and submit again.{where}\n")
432:             reason = f"no submission passed the harness's checks; the last: {'; '.join(result.problems)}"
433:         failures.append(reason or "no passing submission")
434:         (ws.root / "failure.txt").write_text(failures[-1])
435:     raise DesignerFailed(f"chain {chain}, experiment {experiment}: both designer cycles failed:\n" +
436:                          "\n".join(f"- cycle {i + 1}: {r}" for i, r in enumerate(failures)))
437: 
438: 
439: def designer_spawner(*, agent_root: Path, backend: Optional[str] = "opencode", model: Optional[str] = DESIGNER_MODEL,
440:                      sandbox: bool = True, network: bool = False, shell_dir: Optional[Path] = None) -> SpawnFn:
441:     """The real spawner: one sandboxed coding agent session per call, reading the context and
442:     inputs, writing only ``work/``; without network as the closed loop's agents
443:     (`src.rsa.loop.no_network`)."""
444:     from src.runtime.coding_agent import run_coding_agent, select_backend
445: 
446:     env = None
447:     if not network:
448:         from src.rsa.loop import no_network
449: 
450:         if select_backend(backend) != "opencode":
451:             raise ValueError("agents without network are implemented for the opencode backend only")
452:         if shell_dir is None:
453:             raise ValueError("agents without network need shell_dir for their shell wrapper")
454:         bash = shutil.which("bash")
455:         if bash is None:
456:             raise FileNotFoundError("no bash on PATH for the agents' shell wrapper")
457:         wrapper = no_network.write_shell_wrapper(Path(shell_dir), sys.executable, bash)
458:         no_network.verify_wrapper(wrapper, sys.executable)
459:         env = dict(os.environ)
460:         env["SHELL"] = str(wrapper)
461:         env["OPENCODE_PERMISSION"] = no_network.opencode_permission(env.get("OPENCODE_PERMISSION"))
462: 
463:     def spawn(ws: Workspace, prompt: str, timeout_sec: int, log: Path) -> bool:
464:         ok, _ = run_coding_agent(prompt, cwd=agent_root, log_path=log,
465:                                  allowed_dirs=[ws.context, ws.inputs, ws.root / "checks"],
466:                                  writable_dirs=[ws.work], timeout_secs=timeout_sec, backend=backend, model=model,
467:                                  usage_label="rsa_open:designer", stock=True, sandbox=sandbox, env=env)
468:         if not network:
469:             from src.rsa.loop.no_network import web_tool_uses
470: 
471:             used = web_tool_uses(log)
472:             if used:
473:                 raise RuntimeError(f"{ws.root}: the designer used the web although its web tools are denied "
474:                                    f"(a harness bug): {used[:3]}")
475:         return ok
476: 
477:     return spawn

"""One designer cycle (docs/auto_open/PLAN.md §4): the brief, the agent, the harness's checks of
what it submits, the pilot, and the frozen paradigm.

**A cycle** (`run_designer`): the harness lays out a workspace (`prepare_workspace`: the design
context with the floor's reference already scored, the spec's schema, the link library, the
chain's earlier paradigms) and spawns the designer agent (Gemini 4, `DESIGNER_MODEL`) with the
brief (`brief`). The agent works with the tools (`src.rsa_open.tools`) and submits a spec. The
harness then checks the submission itself (`check_submission`), never trusting the agent's
reports:
1. the spec validates and is the one submitted (its sha256);
2. its design is re-scored with a seed of the harness's own, and must meet the floor; this is
   the design that runs;
3. its link is re-checked for recovery in the paradigm, with the harness's seed;
4. its trial lists are built and piloted with LLM participants (`src.rsa_open.pilot`).
A submission that fails any step goes back to the agent with the report, in a new session on the
same workspace (its notes and drafts are still in ``work/``), up to ``MAX_SUBMISSIONS`` (3) per
cycle; a spec that already failed is refused unchanged. A cycle also ends when the agent's
wall-clock budget (``CYCLE_SECONDS``, 2 hours over its sessions) or its tool calls (40) are spent,
or when a session ends without a new submission.

**A failed cycle gets one retry** (PI 2026-10-21), on a fresh workspace with the failure's
reason in the brief; a second failure raises `DesignerFailed` and the chain stops. There is no
fallback design.

**The frozen paradigm** (`freeze`): ``frozen/`` holds the paradigm, its design (the harness's
re-score), the trial lists, the page, the link check, the pilot and ``record.json`` (hashes,
chain, experiment, and ``review_required``: the PI reviews the first paradigm of each chain).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

import numpy as np

from src.rsa_open.timing import CLOSED_CAMPAIGN, TimingRecord, digest_md, write_records
from src.rsa_open.tools import MAX_TOOL_CALLS, Workspace, seed_for

DESIGNER_MODEL = "google/gemini-4-argon"
CYCLE_SECONDS = 2 * 3600
MAX_SUBMISSIONS = 3
MAX_CYCLES = 2
MIN_SESSION_SECONDS = 300  # a session shorter than this is not started
TOOL_SHELL_TIMEOUT_MS = 1_800_000  # link-check fits three models; eig can take minutes
TOOLS_COMMAND = sys.executable + " -m src.rsa_open.tools"
SpawnFn = Callable[[Workspace, str, int, Path], bool]  # (workspace, prompt, timeout_sec, log) -> ok


class DesignerFailed(RuntimeError):
    """Both cycles failed: the chain stops (no fallback design)."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EarlierParadigm:
    """An earlier paradigm of the chain, as the designer sees it: the spec and per-theory fits."""

    name: str
    spec_path: Path
    fits_md: str  # a table of each live theory's fit to that paradigm's data (no participant data)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- the workspace

def links_md() -> str:
    from src.rsa_open.links import LINKS, likelihood

    lines = ["# The link library", "",
             "Each link scores one response type. Every link has a decision `temperature` (sharpens or "
             "flattens the theory's probabilities) and a `lapse` (a uniform guess); some have more. "
             "Their parameters are fitted jointly with the theories', shared by every theory on the "
             "paradigm. The paradigm fixes the options (scale points, total points).", ""]
    for name, link in LINKS.items():
        lk = likelihood(name, scale_points=5, total_points=100)
        priors = ", ".join(f"`{k}` ~ {type(d).__name__}" for k, d in lk.params.items())
        lines += [f"## `{name}` (response type `{link.response_type}`)", "", link.description, "",
                  f"Parameters: {priors}.", ""]
    lines += ["The EIG tool scores every response type. Two are scored on a coarser view of the response, "
              "so their score is a lower bound: a slider binned into 12 outcomes, and a bet as a bet of at "
              "most 10 points (a random part of a bet is a smaller bet).", ""]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def format_example() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """A spec that shows the format only: placeholder content, not a suggestion."""
    square = '<rect x="35" y="35" width="30" height="30" fill="#777777"/>'
    return {
        "schema_version": 1, "name": "FORMAT EXAMPLE ONLY", "summary": "Placeholder text showing the format.",
        "charter": {"question": "Placeholder: the question about pragmatic reference this paradigm asks."},
        "instructions": {"welcome": "Placeholder welcome.", "task": "Placeholder task description.",
                         "comprehension_checks": [{"question": "Placeholder question?",
                                                   "options": ["right option", "wrong option"], "correct": 0}]},
        "materials": {"kind": "svg", "domains": [{"name": "things", "base": '<circle cx="50" cy="50" r="40" fill="#dddddd"/>',
                                                  "features": [{"word": w, "svg": square} for w in ("alpha", "beta")]}]},

  social evaluation of speakers; anything needing deception or emotionally charged material.

You are the experiment designer of chain `{chain}`, experiment {experiment}, in a study of how

## What a paradigm is

A paradigm is one JSON spec: schema `{ws.inputs / 'paradigm_schema.json'}`, a format example (placeholder

**Materials people can read, and want to look at.** Scenes include objects with no features, and
